paper_metadata.title: Towards practical Quantum Credit Risk Analysis

summary: The paper extends the quantum credit risk analysis algorithm using iterative quantum amplitude estimation to support multi‑factor risk models and non‑integer LGD values. A toy experiment with 2 assets and 2 risk factors was simulated on the Qiskit qasm simulator using 9 qubits, ~50,000 quantum samples, target precision ε = 0.002, and 99% confidence to estimate VaR at α = 0.95. No real‑hardware results or runtime comparisons with classical Monte Carlo were reported.

experiments.description: Simulation study of an enhanced quantum credit risk analysis circuit using iterative quantum amplitude estimation with a multi-factor uncertainty model and non-integer LGD values, evaluated on a toy 2-asset, 2-risk-factor instance.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) applied to credit risk analysis with multi-factor uncertainty model
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision epsilon = 0.002 and 99% target confidence interval

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two qubits encode each latent normal risk factor Z1 and Z2; asset default qubits are controlled by linear rotations. The paper also proposes a LinearAmplitudeFunction-based replacement for the S operator to avoid integer-only LGD constraints, but the reported experiment uses the multiple-rotations variant without the sum register.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR at confidence level alpha = 0.95 for portfolio loss distribution, then compute economic capital as VaR_alpha - E[L].
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Bisection search over loss threshold x; objective qubit flipped when cumulative loss is less than or equal to x. No penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Toy credit portfolio with 2 assets and 2 systemic risk factors, used to validate the proposed multi-factor and non-integer LGD improvements.

dataset_specification.description: Parameters given in Table 1: asset 1 LGD 1000.5, p0 0.15, rho 0.1, weights (0.35, 0.2); asset 2 LGD 2000.5, p0 0.25, rho 0.05, weights (0.1, 0.25).

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit supplied to IQAE in Qiskit; bisection search used to find VaR at alpha = 0.95; target precision and confidence interval specified; experiment simulated on qasm simulator.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Iterative quantum amplitude estimation with classical bisection search
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Bisection search over VaR threshold using IQAE estimates; expected loss and VaR used to assess economic capital.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation / iterative quantum amplitude estimation in credit risk analysis
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic speedup as a property of amplitude estimation; the reported experiment is a simulator study and does not empirically benchmark runtime against classical Monte Carlo.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo for amplitude estimation; IQAE avoids QPE and still provides quadratic speedup.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(sqrt(n)) Monte Carlo convergence rate as stated in the paper.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not provided; expected very large because the demonstrated instance uses only 2 assets and 2 risk factors.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large fault‑tolerant quantum computers with many more qubits and long coherence times; the paper notes that current hardware noise destroys results and that meaningful scaling would require thousands of assets and significantly more qubits.
limiting_factors: Only simulator experiments on a toy instance (2 assets, 2 risk factors).
Algorithm relies on amplitude estimation with quadratic speedup only.
Circuit depth and qubit requirements increase significantly with assets and risk factors.
Current hardware noise prevents successful execution on real QPUs.
Data loading circuits for probability distributions and linear amplitude functions add significant overhead.

notes: circuit_depth not explicitly reported; only resource scaling discussion is given, so left null/inferred not used.
num_shots inferred from 'average of approximately 50000 quantum samples' used by IQAE.
hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the experiment was simulated on the qasm simulator backend provided by Qiskit.
The authors mention the theoretical quadratic speedup of amplitude estimation but do not experimentally demonstrate quantum advantage.
All reported experiments are classical simulations (Qiskit qasm simulator) on a very small toy model.
